label: input j at original position 2 or 3
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter j and it sits at original-phase position t=2 or t=3 (precision 1.0). Strongest at t=2 (up to 0.925, e.g. e i [j]), slightly weaker at t=3 (~0.75-0.85). Very weak (~0.04) traces for j at t=1 or t=4, and essentially never at t=0, t>=5, the delimiter, or the copy phase (a handful of copy-phase activations). Not modulated by L, preceding tokens, or whether j repeats. Does not fire on any other token.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.960, F1 0.980, mass recall 0.997, with 0 false positives.

All 1358 test misses are faint activations (about 0.04-0.07) on j at t=1 or t=4. Together they hold 0.3% of the activation mass, which matches the explanation. Adding t=1 and t=4 to the predicate drops precision to 0.54 (F1 0.70), so leaving them out is correct.
Splitting by position, j at t=2 holds 52% of the mass on 48.4% of the active steps and j at t=3 holds 47.6% on 47.6%. So t=2 is slightly stronger per activation, which supports 'strongest at t=2'.
Copy phase: 42 dev activations (all at t=5 with L=3) and 0 on the test split. Delimiter: 0. t=0 and t>=6: 0. The 'essentially never fires' claim holds.
Every activation in the profile is on input j (the by-token table shows all 34403 on j), so 'never fires on any token other than j' holds.
